title: Cable Modem vs DSL: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: There are two classic ways to get internet into a home. One shares a big pipe with the neighbours. The other has its own private line.

scenes.heading: Shared pipe or private pipe
scenes.narration: Think of water coming into a street. With cable, one big main pipe feeds the whole street. With D S L, every house gets its own pipe to the water company. But D S L slows down the further your house is from the exchange. And cable can slow down when everyone is online at the same time.

items.real: Your own line to the exchange

scenes.heading: Cable vs DSL
scenes.narration: Here are the key facts. Cable uses coaxial and shares it, while D S L uses the phone line on its own. At the provider, cable ends on a C M T S, and D S L ends on a D S L A M. Cable follows the DOCSIS standard, and D S L often logs in using P P P o E.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three things to remember. D S L is dedicated, not shared. Its speed drops the further you are from the exchange. And the C M T S is for cable, while the D S L A M is for D S L.

items.wrong: DSL speed is the same everywhere

items.right: CMTS is cable; DSLAM is DSL

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva cable and DSL lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Cable shares bandwidth, and D S L has its own line. D S L slows down with distance. C M T S means cable, and D S L A M means D S L. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva cable and DSL lab.
